title: Marbury v. Madison
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: William Marbury (petitioner seeking writ of mandamus for his commission)
outcome: Writ denied. Marbury had a right to the commission, but §13 of the Judiciary Act of 1789 conferring original mandamus jurisdiction was unconstitutional; the Court could not issue the writ. Established judicial review.

title: McCulloch v. Maryland
court: Supreme Court of the United States
topic: Federal power / Necessary and Proper Clause
plaintiff: James McCulloch, cashier of the Bank of the United States (appellant challenging Maryland's tax)
outcome: Reversed. Congress had implied power to charter the bank; Maryland could not tax it. Judgment for McCulloch.

title: Gibbons v. Ogden
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Thomas Gibbons (appellant, holder of federal coasting license)
defendant: Aaron Ogden (holder of New York steamboat monopoly)
outcome: Reversed. Federal coasting license preempted New York's monopoly; Congress's commerce power includes navigation. Injunction against Gibbons dissolved.

title: Dred Scott v. Sandford
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Dred Scott (enslaved man suing for freedom)
outcome: Scott lost. Held that persons of African descent were not citizens and could not sue in federal court; Missouri Compromise unconstitutional. Later repudiated by the 13th and 14th Amendments.

title: Plessy v. Ferguson
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Homer Plessy (challenging conviction under Louisiana Separate Car Act)
defendant: Judge John Ferguson / State of Louisiana
outcome: Affirmed. Separate-but-equal accommodations upheld under the 14th Amendment. Overruled by Brown v. Board (1954).

title: Lochner v. New York
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Joseph Lochner (bakery owner challenging conviction under maximum-hours law)
outcome: Reversed. The Bakeshop Act's 60-hour limit violated liberty of contract under the Due Process Clause.

title: Schenck v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
topic: Free speech / clear and present danger
plaintiff: Charles Schenck (appealing Espionage Act conviction)
outcome: Affirmed. Distributing anti-draft leaflets in wartime presented a clear and present danger; conviction upheld.

title: Gitlow v. New York
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Benjamin Gitlow (appealing criminal anarchy conviction)
outcome: Affirmed. Free speech applies to the states via the 14th Amendment, but the conviction for publishing the Left Wing Manifesto was upheld.

title: Buck v. Bell
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Carrie Buck (challenging sterilization order)
defendant: J.H. Bell, Superintendent of Virginia State Colony
outcome: Affirmed. Virginia's compulsory sterilization statute upheld; 'three generations of imbeciles are enough.'

title: Near v. Minnesota
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Jay Near (publisher enjoined under Public Nuisance Law)
outcome: Reversed. The gag law authorizing prior restraint on 'malicious, scandalous' newspapers violated the First Amendment.

title: Wickard v. Filburn
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Roscoe Filburn (farmer challenging wheat quota penalty)
outcome: Reversed in favor of the government. Home-grown wheat, in the aggregate, substantially affects interstate commerce; the quota penalty was valid.

title: Korematsu v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Fred Korematsu (appealing conviction for violating exclusion order)
outcome: Affirmed. Exclusion of Japanese Americans upheld as a military necessity. Repudiated in Trump v. Hawaii (2018).

title: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. (steel companies seeking injunction against seizure)
outcome: Affirmed injunction. President Truman lacked constitutional or statutory authority to seize the steel mills.

title: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Oliver Brown and other parents of Black schoolchildren
defendant: Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas
outcome: Reversed. Racially segregated public schools are inherently unequal and violate the Equal Protection Clause; Plessy overruled as to public education.

title: Mapp v. Ohio
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Dollree Mapp (appealing conviction based on warrantless search)
outcome: Reversed. Evidence obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment is inadmissible in state courts.

title: Baker v. Carr
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Charles Baker and Tennessee voters challenging malapportionment
defendant: Joe Carr, Tennessee Secretary of State
outcome: Reversed and remanded. Legislative apportionment claims under the Equal Protection Clause are justiciable, not political questions.

title: Engel v. Vitale
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Steven Engel and other parents
outcome: Reversed. State-composed voluntary school prayer violates the Establishment Clause.

title: Gideon v. Wainwright
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Clarence Earl Gideon (habeas petitioner denied appointed counsel)
outcome: Reversed. States must provide counsel to indigent felony defendants; Betts v. Brady overruled.

title: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: New York Times Co. (appealing libel judgment)
defendant: L.B. Sullivan, Montgomery public safety commissioner
outcome: Reversed. Public officials must prove actual malice to recover for defamation; $500,000 judgment set aside.

title: Heart of Atlanta Motel, Inc. v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Heart of Atlanta Motel (challenging Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964)
outcome: Affirmed. Congress could bar racial discrimination in public accommodations under the Commerce Clause; the motel lost.

title: Griswold v. Connecticut
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Estelle Griswold (Planned Parenthood director appealing conviction)
outcome: Reversed. Connecticut's ban on contraceptive use by married couples violated a constitutional right to marital privacy.

title: Miranda v. Arizona
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Ernesto Miranda (appealing conviction based on unwarned confession)
outcome: Reversed. Suspects must be warned of their rights before custodial interrogation; the confession was inadmissible.

title: Loving v. Virginia
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Richard and Mildred Loving (challenging anti-miscegenation convictions)
outcome: Reversed. Virginia's ban on interracial marriage violated the Equal Protection and Due Process Clauses.

title: Katz v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Charles Katz (appealing conviction based on phone-booth eavesdropping)
outcome: Reversed. The Fourth Amendment protects people, not places; warrantless electronic eavesdropping on a phone booth was an unconstitutional search.

title: Terry v. Ohio
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: John Terry (appealing weapons conviction after stop and frisk)
outcome: Affirmed. A brief stop and protective frisk on reasonable suspicion is permissible; the conviction stood.

title: Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Mary Beth and John Tinker (students suspended for wearing armbands)
defendant: Des Moines Independent Community School District
outcome: Reversed. Students retain free-speech rights absent substantial disruption; the armband suspension was unconstitutional.

title: Brandenburg v. Ohio
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Clarence Brandenburg (KKK leader appealing criminal syndicalism conviction)
outcome: Reversed. Speech may be punished only if directed to inciting imminent lawless action and likely to produce it.

title: New York Times Co. v. United States (Pentagon Papers)
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: United States (seeking injunction against publication)
defendant: New York Times Co. and Washington Post
outcome: Injunctions denied. The government did not meet the heavy burden required to justify a prior restraint on publishing the Pentagon Papers.

title: Lemon v. Kurtzman
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Alton Lemon and taxpayers challenging aid to parochial schools
defendant: David Kurtzman, Pennsylvania Superintendent of Public Instruction
outcome: Reversed. State salary supplements to parochial school teachers created excessive entanglement and violated the Establishment Clause (Lemon test).

title: Furman v. Georgia
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: William Furman (challenging death sentence)
outcome: Reversed. Death sentences imposed under standardless discretionary schemes were cruel and unusual; existing capital statutes invalidated.

title: Roe v. Wade
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Jane Roe (challenging Texas abortion statute)
defendant: Henry Wade, Dallas County District Attorney
outcome: Affirmed in part. Texas's criminal abortion ban violated the right to privacy under the Due Process Clause; trimester framework adopted. Overruled by Dobbs (2022).

title: Miller v. California
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Marvin Miller (appealing conviction for mailing obscene material)
outcome: Vacated and remanded. The Court announced the three-part Miller test for obscenity and sent the case back for reconsideration under it; neither side won outright.

title: United States v. Nixon
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: United States (Special Prosecutor seeking White House tapes)
outcome: Affirmed. Executive privilege is qualified; the subpoena for the tapes must be obeyed.

title: Gregg v. Georgia
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Troy Gregg (challenging death sentence under revised Georgia statute)
outcome: Affirmed. The death penalty is not per se unconstitutional; Georgia's guided-discretion statute satisfied the Eighth Amendment.

title: Buckley v. Valeo
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: James Buckley and others challenging the Federal Election Campaign Act
defendant: Francis Valeo, Secretary of the Senate
outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part. Contribution limits and disclosure upheld; limits on independent expenditures and candidate spending struck down.

title: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Allan Bakke (rejected medical school applicant)
defendant: Regents of the University of California
outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part. The rigid racial quota was unlawful and Bakke was ordered admitted, but race may be considered as one factor in admissions.

title: Chevron U.S.A. Inc. v. Natural Resources Defense Council
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Chevron U.S.A. (petitioner defending EPA's 'bubble' rule)
outcome: Reversed. Courts defer to an agency's reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous statute; EPA's bubble rule upheld. Chevron deference overruled by Loper Bright (2024).

title: New Jersey v. T.L.O.
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: State of New Jersey (seeking to reinstate delinquency finding)
outcome: Reversed. School officials need only reasonable suspicion, not probable cause or a warrant; the purse search was reasonable.

title: Batson v. Kentucky
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: James Batson (challenging conviction after prosecutor struck all Black jurors)
outcome: Reversed and remanded. Peremptory strikes based on race violate the Equal Protection Clause; defendant may make a prima facie showing from his own trial.

title: Bowers v. Hardwick
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Michael Hardwick (challenging Georgia sodomy statute)
defendant: Michael Bowers, Attorney General of Georgia
outcome: Reversed in favor of Georgia. No fundamental right to engage in homosexual sodomy; statute upheld. Overruled by Lawrence v. Texas (2003).

title: Hazelwood School District v. Kuhlmeier
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Hazelwood School District (appealing ruling for student journalists)
defendant: Cathy Kuhlmeier and student staff of the Spectrum newspaper
outcome: Reversed. Educators may exercise editorial control over school-sponsored publications for legitimate pedagogical reasons.

title: Texas v. Johnson
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: State of Texas (seeking to reinstate flag desecration conviction)
outcome: Affirmed. Burning the flag as political protest is protected expressive conduct; the conviction could not stand.

title: Cruzan v. Director, Missouri Department of Health
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Nancy Cruzan's parents (seeking removal of feeding tube)
outcome: Affirmed. A competent person has a liberty interest in refusing treatment, but Missouri may require clear and convincing evidence of an incompetent patient's wishes.

title: Planned Parenthood of Southeastern Pennsylvania v. Casey
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Planned Parenthood (challenging Pennsylvania Abortion Control Act)
outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part. Roe's core holding reaffirmed under an undue-burden standard; spousal notification struck down, other provisions (waiting period, informed consent, parental consent) upheld.

title: Lucas v. South Carolina Coastal Council
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: David Lucas (beachfront lot owner barred from building)
outcome: Reversed and remanded. A regulation depriving land of all economically beneficial use is a per se taking requiring compensation unless background principles of property law would bar the use.

title: United States v. Lopez
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: United States (seeking to reinstate Gun-Free School Zones Act conviction)
outcome: Affirmed. Possessing a gun in a school zone is not economic activity substantially affecting interstate commerce; the Act exceeded Congress's commerce power.

title: Romer v. Evans
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Richard Evans and others challenging Colorado Amendment 2
outcome: Affirmed. Amendment 2, barring anti-discrimination protections for gay people, lacked a rational relationship to a legitimate purpose and violated equal protection.

title: United States v. Virginia (VMI)
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: United States (challenging Virginia Military Institute's male-only admissions)
outcome: Reversed. VMI's exclusion of women violated equal protection; Virginia lacked an exceedingly persuasive justification, and the parallel women's program was no remedy.

title: Clinton v. Jones
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Paula Jones (civil suit against the sitting President)
outcome: Affirmed. A sitting President has no temporary immunity from civil litigation for unofficial conduct; the suit could proceed.

title: Bush v. Gore
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: George W. Bush (seeking to halt Florida recount)
outcome: Reversed. Florida's standardless manual recount violated equal protection and no constitutional recount could be completed by the safe-harbor deadline; recount ended.

title: Lawrence v. Texas
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: John Lawrence and Tyron Garner (challenging convictions under Texas Homosexual Conduct law)
outcome: Reversed. The statute criminalizing private consensual same-sex intimacy violated the Due Process Clause; Bowers overruled.

title: Grutter v. Bollinger
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Barbara Grutter (rejected law school applicant)
defendant: Lee Bollinger, President of the University of Michigan
outcome: Affirmed. The law school's narrowly tailored, individualized consideration of race to achieve diversity survived strict scrutiny. Effectively overruled by SFFA v. Harvard (2023).

title: Kelo v. City of New London
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Susette Kelo and homeowners (challenging condemnation for economic development)
outcome: Affirmed. Taking private property for a comprehensive economic development plan qualifies as public use under the Fifth Amendment.

title: Hamdan v. Rumsfeld
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Salim Hamdan (Guantanamo detainee challenging military commission)
outcome: Reversed. The military commissions violated the UCMJ and the Geneva Conventions; Hamdan could not be tried before them as constituted.

title: District of Columbia v. Heller
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: District of Columbia (defending handgun ban and trigger-lock requirement)
outcome: Affirmed. The Second Amendment protects an individual right to keep a handgun in the home for self-defense; D.C.'s ban was unconstitutional.

title: Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Citizens United (nonprofit barred from airing 'Hillary: The Movie')
outcome: Reversed in part. Limits on independent political expenditures by corporations and unions violate the First Amendment; disclosure requirements upheld.

title: National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: National Federation of Independent Business and 26 states (challenging the ACA)
defendant: Kathleen Sebelius, Secretary of Health and Human Services
outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part. Individual mandate upheld as a tax (not under the Commerce Clause); Medicaid expansion's funding threat was unconstitutionally coercive.

title: Shelby County v. Holder
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Shelby County, Alabama (challenging preclearance coverage formula)
outcome: Reversed. Section 4(b)'s coverage formula was unconstitutional as based on decades-old data; preclearance became inoperative.

title: Riley v. California
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: David Riley (challenging warrantless search of his cell phone)
outcome: Reversed. Police generally need a warrant to search the digital contents of a cell phone seized incident to arrest.

title: Burwell v. Hobby Lobby Stores, Inc.
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Sylvia Burwell, Secretary of HHS (defending contraceptive mandate)
outcome: Affirmed. Under RFRA, closely held for-profit corporations could not be required to provide contraceptive coverage contrary to their owners' religious beliefs.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: James Obergefell and other same-sex couples
defendant: Richard Hodges, Ohio Director of Health
outcome: Reversed. The Fourteenth Amendment requires states to license and recognize same-sex marriages.

title: Carpenter v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Timothy Carpenter (challenging warrantless acquisition of cell-site location records)
outcome: Reversed. Acquiring historical cell-site location records is a search generally requiring a warrant.

title: Masterpiece Cakeshop, Ltd. v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Masterpiece Cakeshop and Jack Phillips (challenging Commission's discrimination finding)
outcome: Reversed. The Commission's proceedings showed hostility to the baker's religious beliefs, violating the Free Exercise Clause; the order against him was set aside.

title: Bostock v. Clayton County
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Gerald Bostock (fired after joining a gay softball league)
outcome: Reversed. Firing an employee for being gay or transgender is discrimination 'because of sex' under Title VII.

title: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Thomas Dobbs, Mississippi State Health Officer (defending 15-week ban)
outcome: Reversed. The Constitution confers no right to abortion; Roe and Casey overruled; Mississippi's Gestational Age Act upheld.

title: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association (challenging 'proper cause' licensing)
defendant: Kevin Bruen, Superintendent of New York State Police
outcome: Reversed. New York's proper-cause requirement for concealed carry violated the Second and Fourteenth Amendments; text-and-history test adopted.

title: Students for Fair Admissions v. President and Fellows of Harvard College
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Students for Fair Admissions
defendant: Harvard College and University of North Carolina
outcome: Reversed. Race-conscious admissions programs at Harvard and UNC violated the Equal Protection Clause and Title VI.

title: Trump v. United States
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Donald Trump (seeking dismissal of federal election-interference indictment on immunity grounds)
outcome: Vacated and remanded. Former Presidents have absolute immunity for core constitutional acts and presumptive immunity for other official acts, but none for unofficial acts; the lower court must sort the allegations.

title: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Loper Bright Enterprises (fishing companies challenging industry-funded monitoring rule)
outcome: Vacated and remanded. Chevron overruled; courts must exercise independent judgment on statutory meaning without deferring to agency interpretations.

title: Hawkins v. McGee
court: Supreme Court of New Hampshire
plaintiff: George Hawkins (patient promised a 'hundred percent perfect hand')
outcome: New trial ordered on damages only; the surgeon's guarantee was an enforceable promise and the proper measure is expectation damages (value of the promised hand minus the hand as it was).

title: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.
court: Court of Appeal (England and Wales)
plaintiff: Louisa Carlill (claimant who used the smoke ball and caught influenza)
outcome: Appeal dismissed; judgment for Mrs Carlill for the £100 reward. The advertisement was a unilateral offer accepted by performance.

title: Hadley v. Baxendale
court: Court of Exchequer (England)
plaintiff: Hadley (mill owners seeking lost profits for delayed crankshaft)
outcome: New trial ordered; lost profits were not recoverable because the carrier had no notice the mill would be idle. Damages limited to losses arising naturally or within the parties' contemplation.

title: Palsgraf v. Long Island Railroad Co.
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Helen Palsgraf (injured by falling scales after fireworks explosion)
outcome: Reversed; complaint dismissed. The railroad owed no duty to an unforeseeable plaintiff outside the zone of danger.

title: Donoghue v. Stevenson
court: House of Lords (UK)
topic: Torts / negligence and duty of care
plaintiff: May Donoghue (consumer of ginger beer containing a decomposed snail)
outcome: Appeal allowed. A manufacturer owes a duty of care to the ultimate consumer; the claim could proceed (neighbour principle).

title: MacPherson v. Buick Motor Co.
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Donald MacPherson (injured when a defective wooden wheel collapsed)
outcome: Affirmed. A manufacturer owes a duty of care to remote purchasers regardless of privity; judgment for MacPherson.

title: Vaughan v. Menlove
court: Court of Common Pleas (England)
plaintiff: Vaughan (neighbour whose cottages burned)
defendant: Menlove (who stacked a hayrick that ignited)
outcome: Verdict for the plaintiff upheld. Negligence is judged by an objective reasonable-person standard, not the defendant's best judgment.

title: Rylands v. Fletcher
court: House of Lords (UK)
plaintiff: Fletcher (mine owner whose mines were flooded)
defendant: Rylands (mill owner who built a reservoir)
outcome: Appeal dismissed; Rylands liable. One who brings onto land something likely to do mischief if it escapes is strictly liable for the escape.

title: Overseas Tankship (UK) Ltd v Morts Dock & Engineering Co (The Wagon Mound No 1)
court: Privy Council
plaintiff: Morts Dock & Engineering (wharf owner whose wharf burned)
outcome: Appeal allowed; claim failed. Liability in negligence is limited to reasonably foreseeable damage; fire damage from the oil was not foreseeable.

title: Tarasoff v. Regents of the University of California
court: Supreme Court of California
plaintiff: Parents of Tatiana Tarasoff (murdered by a patient who told his therapist of his intent)
defendant: Regents of the University of California and campus therapists
outcome: Reversed; complaint stated a cause of action. A therapist who determines a patient poses a serious danger to an identifiable victim has a duty to use reasonable care to protect that victim.

title: Liebeck v. McDonald's Restaurants
court: New Mexico Second Judicial District Court
plaintiff: Stella Liebeck (79-year-old burned by coffee served at about 180-190°F)
outcome: Jury verdict for Liebeck: $200,000 compensatory (reduced 20% for her fault) and $2.7 million punitive damages, later reduced by the judge to $480,000; the parties then settled.

title: Summers v. Tice
court: Supreme Court of California
plaintiff: Charles Summers (shot in the eye while hunting)
defendant: Harold Tice and Ernest Simonson (both fired negligently in his direction)
outcome: Affirmed. Where two defendants act negligently and only one caused the harm, the burden shifts to each to prove he did not; both held jointly liable.

title: Lucy v. Zehmer
court: Supreme Court of Virginia
plaintiff: W.O. Lucy (buyer seeking specific performance of a farm sale written on a restaurant check)
outcome: Reversed; specific performance ordered. Contract formation is judged by outward manifestations, not secret intent; the Zehmers' claim of a joke failed.

title: Jacob & Youngs, Inc. v. Kent
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Jacob & Youngs (builder seeking final payment after using non-Reading pipe)
outcome: Reversed; judgment for the builder. The deviation was trivial and innocent; substantial performance entitled the builder to payment less any difference in value.

title: Wood v. Lucy, Lady Duff-Gordon
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Otis Wood (exclusive agent claiming breach of exclusive marketing deal)
outcome: Reversed; the contract was enforceable. The agent's implied promise to use reasonable efforts supplied consideration.

title: Raffles v. Wichelhaus (The Peerless)
court: Court of Exchequer (England)
plaintiff: Raffles (seller of cotton shipped on a ship named Peerless)
defendant: Wichelhaus (buyer who meant a different ship named Peerless)
outcome: Judgment for the defendants. With two ships named Peerless and no meeting of the minds on which was meant, there was no binding contract.

title: Hamer v. Sidway
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Louisa Hamer (assignee of nephew promised $5,000 for abstaining from drinking, smoking, and gambling until 21)
defendant: Franklin Sidway (executor of the uncle's estate)
outcome: Reversed; judgment for the claimant. Forbearance from lawful conduct is valid consideration regardless of benefit to the promisor.

title: Williams v. Walker-Thomas Furniture Co.
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
plaintiff: Ora Williams (buyer resisting repossession of all goods under cross-collateral clause)
outcome: Reversed and remanded. Courts may refuse to enforce unconscionable contracts; the trial court must consider whether the cross-collateral clause was unconscionable.

title: Pierson v. Post
court: Supreme Court of New York
plaintiff: Lodowick Post (hunter pursuing a fox with hounds)
defendant: Jesse Pierson (who killed and took the fox)
outcome: Reversed; judgment for Pierson. Mere pursuit does not confer possession of a wild animal; occupancy requires capture or mortal wounding.

title: International News Service v. Associated Press
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Associated Press (seeking to enjoin INS from copying its news)
outcome: Affirmed injunction. Appropriating a competitor's fresh news for commercial gain is unfair competition (quasi-property in hot news).

title: Meinhard v. Salmon
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: Morton Meinhard (joint venturer excluded from a renewal lease)
outcome: Affirmed as modified. Co-venturers owe the 'punctilio of an honor the most sensitive'; Meinhard was entitled to share in the new lease opportunity.

title: Dodge v. Ford Motor Co.
court: Supreme Court of Michigan
plaintiff: John and Horace Dodge (minority shareholders seeking dividends)
defendant: Ford Motor Co. and Henry Ford
outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part. Ford was ordered to pay a special dividend (a corporation is run primarily for shareholders' profit), but the injunction against expanding the River Rouge plant was reversed under the business judgment rule.

title: Erie Railroad Co. v. Tompkins
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Erie Railroad Co. (appealing a verdict for a trespasser struck by a train)
outcome: Reversed and remanded. There is no federal general common law; federal courts in diversity must apply state substantive law (Pennsylvania's rule on trespassers). Swift v. Tyson overruled.

title: International Shoe Co. v. Washington
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: International Shoe Co. (challenging Washington's jurisdiction to assess unemployment contributions)
outcome: Affirmed. Systematic and continuous in-state salesman activity established 'minimum contacts' so that jurisdiction did not offend fair play and substantial justice.

title: Sony Corp. of America v. Universal City Studios, Inc. (Betamax)
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Universal City Studios and Walt Disney Productions (suing VCR maker for contributory infringement)
outcome: Reversed in favor of Sony. Home time-shifting is fair use, and a device capable of substantial non-infringing uses does not make its maker a contributory infringer.

title: Campbell v. Acuff-Rose Music, Inc.
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Luther Campbell and 2 Live Crew (defending parody of 'Oh, Pretty Woman')
outcome: Reversed and remanded. Commercial parody can be fair use; the appeals court erred in presuming unfairness from commercial character.

title: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
court: Supreme Court of the United States
plaintiff: Sidney Diamond, Commissioner of Patents (seeking to deny patent on a genetically engineered bacterium)
outcome: Affirmed. A live, human-made microorganism is patentable subject matter as a 'manufacture' or 'composition of matter.'

title: R v Dudley and Stephens
court: Queen's Bench Division (England)
plaintiff: The Crown (prosecuting shipwrecked sailors who killed and ate a cabin boy)
outcome: Defendants convicted of murder. Necessity is no defence to murder; death sentences later commuted to six months' imprisonment.

title: M'Naghten's Case
court: House of Lords (UK)
plaintiff: The Crown (prosecuting Daniel M'Naghten for killing Edward Drummond)
outcome: Acquitted by reason of insanity. The Lords then articulated the M'Naghten rules: a defendant is not responsible if, from a defect of reason due to disease of the mind, he did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong.

title: People v. Goetz
court: New York Court of Appeals
plaintiff: People of the State of New York (seeking to reinstate indictment of subway shooter)
outcome: Reversed; indictment reinstated. Justification requires that the defendant's belief in the need for deadly force be objectively reasonable, not merely sincere.

title: United States et al. v. Hermann Göring et al. (Nuremberg Trial of the Major War Criminals)
court: International Military Tribunal, Nuremberg
plaintiff: The Allied prosecution (United States, United Kingdom, USSR, France)
defendant: Hermann Göring and 21 other Nazi leaders
outcome: Nineteen of 22 defendants convicted (12 sentenced to death), three acquitted. Individual criminal responsibility for aggression, war crimes and crimes against humanity established.

title: People v. O.J. Simpson
court: Los Angeles County Superior Court
plaintiff: People of the State of California (prosecuting for the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman)
outcome: Jury acquitted Simpson on both counts of murder after a nine-month trial; the defense argued reasonable doubt from evidence-handling and police credibility problems.

title: State of Tennessee v. John Thomas Scopes (Scopes Monkey Trial)
court: Rhea County Circuit Court, Tennessee
plaintiff: State of Tennessee (prosecuting under the Butler Act)
defendant: John T. Scopes, high school teacher
outcome: Scopes convicted and fined $100. The Tennessee Supreme Court later reversed on the technicality that the jury, not the judge, should have set the fine, but upheld the Act.

title: Trial of Bridget Bishop (Salem witch trials)
court: Court of Oyer and Terminer, Salem, Massachusetts Bay
plaintiff: The Crown / Massachusetts Bay colony (prosecuting for witchcraft on spectral and testimonial evidence)
outcome: Convicted of witchcraft and hanged on June 10, 1692, the first execution of the Salem trials. The convictions were later condemned and reversed by the colony.

title: State of New Jersey v. Bruno Richard Hauptmann (Lindbergh kidnapping)
court: Hunterdon County Court of Oyer and Terminer, New Jersey
plaintiff: State of New Jersey (prosecuting for the kidnapping and murder of Charles Lindbergh Jr.)
outcome: Convicted of first-degree murder and executed in 1936, largely on ransom-money, handwriting and ladder-wood evidence.

title: Brown v. Kendall
court: Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts
plaintiff: George Brown (struck in the eye by a stick while defendant separated fighting dogs)
outcome: New trial ordered in defendant's favor on the law. Liability for unintentional injury requires want of ordinary care; the plaintiff bears the burden of proving negligence.
